context.problemStatement:
Implement the `Lambda` case of `eval`. An anonymous function `fn(x) { ... }`
evaluates to a function value. Nothing in its body is evaluated until it is
called, so this case never returns an error. Build a `VFunc(UserFn(...))` whose
name is `"lambda"` (used in error messages) and whose parent is the environment
in which this function was *defined*, not the one in which it will be called. This
is what lets a function use the names around it, even after the call that created it
has returned.

```
// In eval:
    Lambda(params, body) ->
      // YOUR CODE HERE (replace the code below)
      Error(errors.NotImplemented(
        "Lambda("
        <> string.inspect(params)
        <> ", "
        <> string.inspect(body)
        <> ")",
      ))
```

Run the tests:

```
gleam test -- q8
```

targets.claim: Student can explain why their Lambda case never returns an error even when the body of the anonymous function uses an unbound name, and when such an error would appear instead.

probes.question: If `body` in `Lambda(params, body)` contains an unbound variable, why does evaluating `Lambda` succeed without returning an error, and when would that error actually get raised?
probes.reason: Directly asks the student to explain why constructing the lambda value does not fail on unbound variables in the body and identifies when that error surfaces.

probes.question: In your `eval` case for `Lambda(params, body)`, why do you return `Ok(...)` immediately without calling `eval(body, ...)` or checking `body`, and what would have to happen for an error inside `body` to be detected?
probes.reason: Approaches the claim by pointing out the lack of recursive evaluation of `body` in the `Lambda` branch and asking what trigger causes body errors to show up.

content: If `body` in `Lambda(params, body)` contains an unbound variable, why does evaluating `Lambda` succeed without returning an error, and when would that error actually get raised?
because we didn't apply the variables yet, we just evaluated the body of the lambda, the error would get raised when we use that lambda function
